**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/24 (Wed) 07:27
- [FACT] Knicks Go is a retired Thoroughbred racehorse foaled on January 29, 2016.
- [FACT] Knicks Go was the 2021 American Horse of the Year after winning five of seven starts.
- [FACT] Knicks Go's notable wins include the Breeders' Cup Classic, Whitney Stakes, and Pegasus World Cup.
- [FACT] Knicks Go won the Breeders' Cup Dirt Mile the year before his 2021 victories.
- [FACT] Knicks Go is the sixth horse to win two different Breeders' Cup races.
- [FACT] Knicks Go's other wins include the Breeders' Futurity as a two-year-old in 2018.
- [FACT] Knicks Go finished second in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile.
- [FACT] Knicks Go finished second in the 2022 Pegasus World Cup.
- [FACT] Knicks Go was retired to stud at Taylor Made Farm in Nicholasville, Kentucky.
- [FACT] Knicks Go's initial stud fee was $30,000.
- [FACT] Knicks Go is a gray horse.
- [FACT] Knicks Go was bred by Angie Moore and her daughter Sabrina at GreenMount Farm in Reisterstown, Maryland.
- [FACT] Knicks Go is from the second crop of Paynter, who won the Haskell Invitational.
- [FACT] Paynter received widespread social media attention during his battle against a near-fatal case of colitis and laminitis.
- [FACT] Knicks Go was produced by Kosmo's Buddy, a stakes-winning daughter of Outflanker.
- [FACT] Kosmo's Buddy was claimed by the Moores for $40,000 near the end of a 37-race career.
- [FACT] Knicks Go was sold as a weanling for $40,000 at the 2016 Keeneland November sale.
- [FACT] Knicks Go was resold as a yearling at the Keeneland September 2017 sale for $87,000 to the Korea Racing Authority.
- [FACT] Knicks Go was originally trained by Ben Colebrook and was transferred to the stable of Brad Cox at the end of 2019.
- [FACT] The colt was named for the K-nicks breeding system used by the Korea Racing Authority (KRA).
- [FACT] The "K" in K-nicks stands for Korea, and "nicks" refers to the above-average success of certain sires when bred to mares from certain other sire lines.
- [RELATIONSHIP] Jun Park is mentioned as a racing manager of the KRA.
